description.narrative: Project Outcome: Stakeholder effects - Increased access to finance for suppliers in Mexico: the Project is expected to promote sustainable supply chains and enable access to finance for local suppliers and SME suppliers in Mexico, including the last mile of the supply chain, which is second-tier or deep-tier SME suppliers, at an accelerated pace via participation structure with HSBC. A couple of practical constraints have discouraged the financing of the SCF gaps in EMs: (i) inability to address receivables financing needs from suppliers of non-investment grade buyers; and (ii) manual and fragmented processes, leading to inefficiencies. Approximately 31% of SMEs in Mexico cite a lack of access to funding as a major obstacle to growth. The lack of access to finance in Mexico is even worse for women-owned SMEs, with 35% of them reporting being financially constrained, compared to 28% for men-owned SMEs. To address these gaps, the Project will (i) provide sustainable financial inclusion by covering buyers with climate targets to support their suppliers in EMs to enhance the connectivity to value chains globally; and (ii) facilitate and undertake more SCF and therefore enhance market integration and efficiencies for intraregional trade.Project Outcome: Stakeholder effects - Increased access to finance for suppliers in Mexico: the Project is expected to promote sustainable supply chains and enable access to finance for local suppliers and SME suppliers in Mexico, including the last mile of the supply chain, which is second-tier or deep-tier SME suppliers, at an accelerated pace via participation structure with HSBC. A couple of practical constraints have discouraged the financing of the SCF gaps in EMs: (i) inability to address receivables financing needs from suppliers of non-investment grade buyers; and (ii) manual and fragmented processes, leading to inefficiencies. Approximately 31% of SMEs in Mexico cite a lack of access to funding as a major obstacle to growth

The proposed investment is a risk-sharing facility with HSBC Mexico S.A., Institución de Banca Múltiple, Grupo Financiero (HSBC Mexico) in a portfolio of supply chain finance-related assets for up to US$200 million with IFC investment of up to US$100 million (the Project). The Project falls under the Global Supply Chain Finance (GSCF) Program, a supply chain finance program launched by the International Finance Corporation (IFC) in December 2022. The GSCF supports open account trade in the emerging markets by providing direct loan, funded or unfunded risk participation in partner banks facilities.
